production.note: Build years of the Gullwing coupe (no page opened gives US model years; the record uses build years, which is how these cars are listed, e.g. RM Sotheby's "1957 Mercedes-Benz 300 SL Gullwing"). RM Sotheby's: "more than 1,000 of the 1,400 cars produced between 1954 and early 1957 were delivered through Hoffman" (the US distributor). Automobile-Sportive: "1954-1957" for the Gullwing ("1957-1963" for the Roadster; autosportive-300-sl). The Newport Car Museum gives "1954-1956" (newport-1955-300-sl). The car was sold new in the US, so this is a US-market record. The 300 SL Roadster (W198 II, 1957-1963) is a separate car and not part of this record.

body.note: Gullwing coupe; the open car was sold as the 300 SL Roadster.

aspiration.note: Fuel-injected straight-six with no forced induction mentioned; inferred.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL: an unsigned auction catalogue and an enthusiast article, agreeing. Quote (RM Sotheby's auction catalogue): "240 bhp at 6,100 rpm (SAE) and 215 bhp at 5,800 rpm (DIN)". The 240 is the period US SAE gross rating; the DIN figure is Mercedes-Benz's net rating of 215 PS, used under the batch rule for classic cars (prefer the maker's net figure over SAE gross and mention the gross). Automobile-Sportive (Sébastien Dupuis): "Puissance: 215 / 222 ch à 5800 tr/mn" (Gullwing / Roadster; autosportive-300-sl). 215 PS x 0.98632 = 212 hp. The Newport Car Museum prints "210 hp @ 6,100 rpm" (newport-1955-300-sl), within 1%. Rating unchanged 1954-1957, so the launch year is the reference year.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL: a museum page (enthusiast type) and an enthusiast article. Quote (Newport Car Museum, 1955 300 SL Gullwing): "Curb weight – 2,855 lbs". Automobile-Sportive (Sébastien Dupuis): "Poids (kg): 1295 / 1330" (Gullwing / Roadster; autosportive-300-sl); the figure is not labelled kerb or dry. 1,295 kg x 2.20462 = 2,855 lb, so Newport's figure is very likely the same European 1,295 kg converted rather than an independent US figure. Coupe, 4-speed manual, the only configuration.

discrepancies.reason: Rating standards: 215 is Mercedes-Benz's DIN rating in PS, 240 the period US SAE gross rating; Newport's 210 hp appears to be the DIN figure converted or rounded differently.
discrepancies.resolution: 215 PS (DIN), the maker's net rating, converted to 212 hp; the SAE gross figure is recorded in the note.

provisionalNote: Power and weight are provisional. Power (215 PS DIN = 212 hp) rests on RM Sotheby's unsigned auction catalogue and Automobile-Sportive (enthusiast), agreeing. Weight (2,855 lb, 1,295 kg) rests on the Newport Car Museum page and Automobile-Sportive's unlabelled 1,295 kg, which are probably the same European figure. Production years are build years. A Mercedes-Benz Classic technical data page or period Mercedes-Benz brochure for the 300 SL coupe (W 198 I), or a major magazine spec panel, would replace both.
